turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a call at 4:40, Hale, so this gets twenty minutes. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
Don't manage me, Hale. I'm not upset, I'm on a clock. You entered a mark before a single phone call to me, so tell me what you were looking at when you did it.
But I'm not changing the grade.

Then I'll hear the basis before I go upstairs. Your own procedure, 4.2, says I get called before any mark goes in, and 4.3 says software alone doesn't establish anything. So what else do you have, or is the principal my next stop?
I'm still not changing it. Keep going if you like.

I'm writing down that you won't change it and won't tell me why. Is anything on Owen's record right now, yes or no? Because when we're done here, I'm walking straight to the principal's office with your policy in my hand.
You can say it ten more ways. The answer is no.
No to what, Hale, the mark or his record? I want that answer precise, because I'll be repeating it to the principal word for word. And I'll want it in an email tonight.
